title: Existence of a base for a finite reduced rational root pairing
statement: Let $M,N$ be vector spaces over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field], let $I$ be finite, and let $P:\operatorname{RootPairing}\ I\ \mathbf Q\ M\ N$ be a reduced crystallographic root pairing in the Mathlib sense. Explicitly, $M,N$ have a perfect bilinear pairing $\langle-,-\rangle$ (the induced maps to the linear duals are isomorphisms), injective root and coroot families $a_i\in M$, $b_i\in N$ with $\langle a_i,b_i\rangle=2$, integral mutual pairings, and simultaneous permutations induced by the reflections $x\mapsto x-\langle x,b_i\rangle a_i$ and $y\mapsto y-\langle a_i,y\rangle b_i$. Assume both families span their respective vector spaces, and that any two linearly dependent roots are equal or negatives of each other. Then $P.\operatorname{Base}$ is inhabited: there exists a finite support $J\subseteq I$ such that the roots indexed by $J$ are linearly independent, the coroots indexed by $J$ are linearly independent, and every root, respectively coroot, or its negative is a sum with nonnegative integer coefficients of its respective family indexed by $J$. Here linear independence and bases use [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. This permits $I=J=\varnothing$ and $M=N=0$.
